[QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | Ibn Majah transmits that whoever renews the istirja when recalling an old calamity receives the same reward as on the day it occurred.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قيل | reports | Another view says innā lillāh expresses present acceptance of what happened, while innā ilayhi rājiʿūn expresses acceptance of whatever will happen later.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The verse contains an obligation to submit to God's command and decree and patiently perform duties, plus a voluntary act of voicing istirjāʿ.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Voicing istirjāʿ has benefits, including angering disbelievers by displaying seriousness in obedience to God's commands and avoidance of prohibitions.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p60/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The Prophet is to give glad tidings to Muslims who patiently accept God's decree in belief and speech, confessing that they are God's servants and return to Him.

[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · أبوه | reports | A report transmitted by Hishām from his father says Abū Bakr gathered the Qur’an after the Prophet; Ibn Kathir calls the report sound as well.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | After Qur’an reciters were killed in large numbers at Yamāma, ʿUmar urged Abū Bakr to collect the Qur’an lest it be lost as its memorizers died in battle; Abū Bakr hesitated, then agreed, as did Zayd.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | At Yamāma, the Muslim army was initially shaken by the much larger force; about three thousand reciters regrouped, cried out to the Companions of al-Baqara, and fought until victory, though about five hundred reciters died.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Ibn Kathir calls this episode one of Zayd ibn Thābit’s greatest merits: Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and Zayd agreed to preserve the Qur’an in writing so it would not disappear with the deaths of memorizers.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · عمر بن الخطاب | reports | Al-Ḥasan reports that ʿUmar asked about a Qur’anic verse, learned that its bearer had been killed at Yamāma, and ordered the Qur’an gathered; the report calls this the first collection in a codex.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p467/r7] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The patient console themselves with this confession: they belong to God, who disposes of His servants as He wills, and return to Him in the afterlife, where not even an atom’s weight is lost; this acknowledges their servanthood and return.

[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p468/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · أم سلمة | reports | Umm Salama reports that after Abū Salama died she made the prescribed supplication, doubting anyone could be better; after her waiting period the Prophet married her, addressed her concerns about jealousy, age, and dependents, and she regarded him as God’s better replacement.
